transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function using an explicit `slice: &[T]` receiver parameter, named return, and the source `F: FnMut(&T) -> K` / `K: PartialOrd` bounds.

Represented the Rust `self.iter().is_sorted_by_key(f)` chain as `self_slice.iter().is_sorted_by_key(f)` over a target-local SliceReceiver/Iter wrapper, because Verus cannot directly verify the standard slice iterator internals in this harness.

Isolated only the standard iterator traversal, FnMut key-observation trace, and PartialOrd comparison behavior in the target-local `Iter::is_sorted_by_key` external_body boundary; the public target is not external_body and does not assume the target postcondition.
Instantiated the generated `slice_sorted_by_partial_key_result` vocabulary and its FnMut-adjacent-key/PartialOrd helper definitions from the frozen shared slice vocabulary.
Added closed spec views for the target-local receiver and iterator wrappers and revealed them only in ghost proof blocks; these annotations have no executable control-flow or data-flow effect.
